title: Your Brain Feels Prices Like Pain
sources: Knutson, Rick, Wimmer, Prelec & Loewenstein (2007), 'Neural predictors of purchases', Neuron 53(1):147-156 (PMC1876732): 26 people chose whether to buy products in an fMRI scanner; product preference activated the nucleus accumbens, excessive prices activated the insula and deactivated the mesial prefrontal cortex; brain activity predicted purchases above self-report
Stanford FSI summary of the study (fsi.stanford.edu/node/24816)

lines.text: Your brain feels a high price tag like pain.
In two thousand seven, Stanford scientists scanned people's brains while they shopped.
lines.caps: In | 2007,~two | Stanford | scientists | scanned | people's | brains | while they | shopped.

lines.text: First, they saw something they wanted,
and a reward spot deep in the brain lit up.
Too high, and the insula fired, an area linked to pain.
The scans could even predict what people would buy,
So this Black Friday, when a deal feels amazing, remember,
